newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat higher on soybeans plus spring acreage.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat higher on soybeans plus spring acreage.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures were higher at midsession on a rally in soybean futures plus bullish input from an estimate for 1997 U.S. spring wheat acreage.
Traders said Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies Friday pegged 1997 U.S. spring wheat acreage at 18.59 million acres, below the firm's previous outlook for 20.312 million.
The market also was concerned about weather problems in the U.S. spring wheat region of the upper Midwest and there was concern about wet weather in some soft red winter states.
Meteorologists early Friday reported rain in the Ohio River Valley and more than a foot of snow fell from the Dakotas to Wisconsin.
Gains in March were limited by news Sri Lanka bought wheat from Argentina and the EU rather than from the U.S. Also a Philippine firm rejected offers on U.S. wheat and soybeans.
Demand for wheat futures was centered in the July and included E.D. and F. Man Interntional and Refco Inc each with three million bushels bought in the July.
At 1136 CST, wheat was five to seven cents per bushel higher, with March up five at $3.79.
